text: P-Model, an electronic rock band formed in 1979 by members of the defunct progressive rock band Mandrake, has undergone numerous lineup changes over the years but has always been led by frontman Susumu Hirasawa. The band officially disbanded in 2000, though many of its members continue to release solo albums and collaborate on various projects. Hirasawa has since released work under the name "Kaku P-Model" (核P-Model; lit. 'nucleus of P-Model'), effectively marking a solo revival of the band. All videos from the albums *Great Brain* to *Harm Harmonizer* were directed by Yuichi "You1" Hirasawa, Susumu's brother. The tracks "Fu-Ru-He-He-He," "2D or Not 2D," and "Grid" are included in *Bitmap 1979–1992*; "Monotone Grid" in *Photon-3*; "http" in *Rocket Shoot*; and "Logic Airforce" in *Live Video Music Industrial Wastes〜P-Model or Die*. P-Model and Susumu Hirasawa have been influential on both musicians and artists in other mediums, particularly within the manga and anime industries. Several of their collaborators, including six band members, began as major fans of their work: Berserk mangaka Kentaro Miura has stated that listening to Hirasawa's music has helped him refocus on the themes of his writing; anime director Satoshi Kon described Hirasawa's work as "a source of imagination and creativity for me" over the past 20 years; and film director Daihachi Yoshida considers Hirasawa the creator of "about half of my way of thinking." Musicians such as Fukusuke of Metronome, Hiroyuki Hayashi of Polysics, Daoko (whose song "Welcome to the Parade" from 2012's *HyperGirl: Mukōgawa no Onna no Ko* was directly influenced by Hirasawa's worldview), Toby Driver of Kayo Dot (who claims *Plastic House on Base of Sky* was an attempt to create his own version of Hirasawa's music), and Kenshi Yonezu (who said a Hirasawa song "changed [his] life") have cited P-Model or Hirasawa as influences. Other artists who have expressed admiration include Klaha of Malice Mizer, Ryoko Yamagishi of *Shiroi Heya no Futari*, Arika Takarano of Ali Project, Hiroyuki Kitakubo (director of *Roujin Z* and *JoJo's Bizarre Adventure*), Sumire Uesaka, Gen Hoshino, Kouta Hirano (mangaka of *Hellsing*), Koyoharu Gotouge (mangaka of *Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba*), Seiji Mizushima (director of *Fullmetal Alchemist* and *Concrete Revolutio*), Satoshi "hil" Ishikawa (composer of *Fate/stay night [Réalta Nua]* and *Taiko no Tatsujin*), and Ko Shibasaki. The five main characters of the *K-On!* franchise—Yui Hirasawa, Mio Akiyama, Ritsu Tainaka, Tsumugi Kotobuki, and Azusa Nakano—are in a band, share the surnames of late '80s P-Model members, and play their respective primary instruments (except Nakano). All active members referenced have acknowledged this connection. Additionally, P-Model references appear in the manga *The Sorrow of a Perfectly Healthy Girl* and *Opus*, as well as in the anime *Sailor Moon*, *Perfect Blue*, *BECK: Mongolian Chop Squad*, and *Space Dandy*. In theatre, musician/playwright Keralino Sandorovich (ja) named two of his stage plays—*Frozen Beach* and *Blue Cross*—after P-Model songs and one, *Haldyn Hotel*, after a Hirasawa solo song.
